title: Simultaneous transcendental element at finitely many prime fibres
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative ring, let $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_r$ be prime ideals (prime ideals are proper ideals whose quotient is an integral domain) of $B$ such that no $\mathfrak p_i$ is contained in another for $i\ne j$, let $k_i$ be a subfield of the residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-field-extension], and assume each extension $\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)/k_i$ is not algebraic [def-weil-algebraic-element]. If $J\subset B$ is an ideal not contained in any $\mathfrak p_i$, then there exists $x\in J$ whose image in $\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)$ is transcendental over $k_i$ for every $i$ (the assertion is vacuous when $r=0).
